ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline: advanced and metastatic prostate cancer. Leaf-matched throughout, because the conversion again made the journal running head `Annals of Oncology` a parent and promoted several bolded captions; the leaves are the guideline's own section titles and they name the castration state outright.

ESMO writes mCSPC -- metastatic castration-sensitive -- where AUA writes mHSPC, metastatic hormone-sensitive. Same patients, same setting, so mCSPC routes to `prostate_metastatic_hormone_sensitive`. Recording the two vocabularies as one setting is the point of having a setting at all.

**`mCRPC` is a substring of `nmCRPC`, so the non-metastatic rules are stated first.** This is the second document in the corpus to carry that trap -- AUA's advanced prostate guideline has it too -- and it is worth naming twice, because both values are valid and an audit passes either way. Reversed, every non-metastatic castration-resistant recommendation would file under metastatic disease and nothing would complain.

default.note: The document spans castration-sensitive and castration-resistant disease, and its front matter -- incidence, diagnosis, staging, molecular biology -- applies across both.

rules.note: Stated before every mCRPC rule below, because `mcrpc` is a substring of `nmcrpc`. Claims the management chapter and the high-risk nmCRPC section.
Metastatic castration-sensitive disease: de novo and relapsed, metastasis-directed therapy, treatment of the primary tumour, supportive care and follow-up. ESMO's mCSPC is AUA's mHSPC.
Spelled out rather than abbreviated in the biomarker-testing section, so the `mCRPC` needle does not reach it.

Reaches only what the nmCRPC rule above did not claim: biomarker testing, management with and without known genetic alterations, sequencing and combination treatment, aggressive variants, molecularly defined subgroups, metastasis-directed therapy, supportive care and follow-up.

Purpose only. The setting and reason are the document's own default, so this rule changes no routing -- it sits after every rule above it and claims only the 2 passages that were already falling through. `diagnosis` is taken from the heading, which names what the section is for.
